metadata.title: Three-dimensional delayed-detonation models with nucleosynthesis for Type Ia supernovae

metadata.description:
Hydrodynamic data described by Seitenzahl et al. 2013. Please cite the paper when using any of the data.

Time at the end of this simulation:

  • ddt_2013_N1: 100.20s
  • ddt_2013_N10: 100.13s
  • ddt_2013_N100: 100.22s
  • ddt_2013_N100H: 100.00s
  • ddt_2013_N100L: 100.19s
  • ddt_2013_N100_Z0.01: 100.22s
  • ddt_2013_N150: 98.21s
  • ddt_2013_N1600: 100.15s
  • ddt_2013_N1600C: 100.13s
  • ddt_2013_N20: 100.01s
  • ddt_2013_N200: 100.21s
  • ddt_2013_N3: 100.19s
  • ddt_2013_N300C: 100.13s
  • ddt_2013_N40: 100.08s
  • ddt_2013_N5: 100.10s

File format explanation:

  • Spherical average of density profile: <model>_density.dat
    • 2 columns: first column gives the velocity in km/s (specified at the centre of a radial shell), second column gives density in g/cm^3
    • For models that leave a bound remnant, the profile extends only over the ejecta.
    • The density is computed as a spherical average over the hydrodynamics data; thus, it is a good description for the density at the corresponding radius. It may, however, be slightly inconsistent when integrating to obtain a mass.
  • Spherical average of isotopic profile: <model>_isotopes.dat
    • 2 + n columns: first column gives the velocity in km/s (specified at the centre of a radial shell), second column gives density in g/cm^3, next n columns give the mass fractions of the isotopes as given in the first row
    • For models that leave a bound remnant, the profile extends only over the ejecta.
  • Integrated abundances: <model>_abundances.dat
    • This file provides integrated abundances of the ejecta for radioactive isotopes at the end of the simulation, for stable isotopes after about 2 Gyr, and for stable elements after about 2 Gyr.
    • All masses are given in solar masses.
  • Integrated abundances of bound remnant: <model>_abundances_core.dat
    • This file provides integrated abundances of the bound remnant for radioactive isotopes at the end of the simulation, for stable isotopes after about 2 Gyr, and for stable elements after about 2 Gyr.
    • All masses are given in solar masses.
  • Optical spectral time series (angle-averaged): <model>_spectra.dat
    • Table with 1+n columns and 1+m lines specifying the optical spectral time series for n epochs on m wavelength bins.
    • The first line defines the time of the n epochs for which spectra have been calculated (time in days since explosion, the first 0.00 is a dummy value).
    • The following m lines contain the fluxes for the various time steps for a given wavelength bin. The first column gives the wavelength in A, followed by n columns giving the fluxes (in units of erg/cm^2/s/A assuming a distance of 10pc).
  • UVOIR bolometric light curve (angle-averaged): <model>_lightcurve.dat
    • Table with 2 columns: the first column gives the time since explosion in days, the second column gives the integrated UVOIR bolometric luminosity in erg/s
  • Gamma-ray spectral time series (angle-averaged): <model>_spectra_gamma.dat
    • Table with 1+n columns and 1+m lines specifying the gamma-ray spectral time series for n epochs on m energy bins.
    • The first line defines the time of the n epochs for which spectra have been calculated (time in days since explosion, the first 0.00 is a dummy value).
    • The following m lines contain the fluxes for the various time steps for a given energy bin. The first column gives the energy in MeV, followed by n columns giving the fluxes (in units of erg/cm^2/s/Hz assuming a distance of 10pc).
  • Early U, B, V, and R light curve (spherically symmetric): <model>_lightcurves_early.dat
    • One-line header specifying the columns
    • Table with 5 columns: the first column gives the time since explosion in days, the remaining four give the absolute AB-magnitudes in the U, B, V, and R pass bands, respectively.
  • Peak magnitudes and decline rates: <model>_delta_m.dat
    • One-line header specifying the columns
    • Table with three columns: the first column gives the peak bolometric magnitudes for 100 viewing angles, the second and third columns list the corresponding bolometric decline rates over 15 and 40 days, respectively.

Not all the data is available for all models.

The hydrodynamics and yields data provided here are spherically averaged from the 3D models. Thus, inconsistencies with published 3D data can arise (e.g., for the yields), especially for models with large-scale asymmetries, such as pure deflagrations.

references.reference: Seitenzahl, I. R., Ciaraldi-Schoolmann, F., Röpke, F. K., Fink, M., Hillebrandt, W., Kromer, M., Pakmor, R., Ruiter, A. J., Sim, S. A., & Taubenberger, S. (2013): Three-dimensional delayed-detonation models with nucleosynthesis for Type Ia supernovae, Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society, 429, 1156
